The switchbot curtain integration currently hard codes that whenever the curtain is moving, is_opening = True. This means when you close the curtain your switchbot will go to "opening" then "closed" which is confusing. This will now set the opening or closing state based on which command was issued and the direction of trael.

issue_context.title: SwitchBot Curtain incorrectly displays opening state instead of closing
issue_context.body:

As per the title, SwitchBot Curtain incorrectly displays `opening` state instead of `closing` while closing the curtain.

This is with a v1 SwitchBot Curtain, but I assume that this will be the same with the v2 (and v3 once supported). It should be easily reproducible and I suspect is a simple oversight in the integration to change to show `closing` instead of `opening`.

I never actually seen this as a bug but I now remember that this also happens at my HA. So I just checked the code:
```python

        self._attr_is_closed = self.parsed_data["position"] <= 20
        self._attr_is_opening = self.parsed_data["inMotion"]
```
I have the feeling we can't really check which way the curtains go, except for the fact that they open and close. so it's always showing opening when it's moving (in motion) and shows closing when the position is less than 20.

If it's not possible to determine motion direction, could some pseudo logic be applied that they are closing if they were previously `open` or the state changed to show `moving` rather than `opening`? I know it's a minor thing, but it's just a bit jarring to see them showing `opening` when they are in fact `closing`. It seems that the percentage is updated while they are in motion, so if the percentage is decreasing or increasing, then maybe this could be used? They currently show `opening` for me no matter what the percentage position is when the motion is started. Sorry, thought this would be an easy fix.

It's always free to ask :)

I think this is something that's hard to get right. What is the definition of closed? 100%? My curtains are heavy so it doesn't always show a complete 100%. But what do you choose if the curtains are closed halfway. I think the current approach chosen is to do it wrong consistently instead of being weird every time.

About having a state `moving` sounds interesting, I'll have a look if there are more cases where this could be useful

I agree, it's difficult to define what is closed and open and there is definitely a problem with even the SwitchBot app showing the correct state if the curtains don't close to it's determined 100% position as showing Partially Open.

If I were to arbitrarily pick a figure to get around the problem of not always being 100% or 0% when actually fully open or closed, I would assume that >= 90% is open and <= 10% is closed and coming from those positions was either closing or opening. `moving` (or similar) might be a better solution if it's really not possible to determine direction or apply some pseudo logic, assuming it's allowed to introduce it as a state for a cover. At least that way it's never incorrect. :-)
Just wondering if this is the same for the SwitchBot Blind Tilt. I don't have any of them yet, but considering purchasing a few.
FWIW `moving` was just the first verb that came into my head that was position agnositic. Other options could be `adjusting` `repositioning`, `operating` etc.

I just saw you suggested the same thing. I'm going to take a stab this weekend at seeing if that's possible

I submitted a PR that should resolve the issue. The only thing I don't have to test with is an open-from-center curtain, but I tested opening from left and from right and it works fine. 
1. If there is a position move reported it will use that to update the direction. However, I noticed several times where it would go from 100 -> 0, no intermediary updates. Not sure why that is. Other times I'd get multiple position updates while it was moving. So bullet 2 handles the situation where the updated reports go from 100->0 or 0->100 directly.
2. When you run an open or close service call it uses that information to know whether it should set opening/closing (other integrations do this same thing)
3. Similarly, using a set position service call will calculate the direction and trigger opening/closing directly

Still working on this, got some good feedback on the PR that required making a change to pySwitchbot library first. So need to wait for that to be approved and a new version to be released to them update HA to point to that new version of the library.
